data.logic_rule:
let queue = input.queue || []
let decision = input.i < queue.length ? 'next' : 'done'
decision

let queue = input.queue || []
let current = queue[input.i] || null
current

let c = input.current
let decision = c && c.id ? 'yes' : 'no'
decision

questions.instructions: Which team should handle this support message? Choose the single best fit for what the customer actually needs resolved.

options.description: Payments, invoices, charges, refunds, pricing or what a subscription costs.
options.name: billing

options.description: The product is broken or misbehaving: crashes, errors, outages, bugs, corrupted or missing data.
options.name: technical

options.description: The customer cannot get into their account: login failures, password resets, lockouts, two-factor problems.
options.name: account_access

options.description: None of the above — sales enquiries, job applications, partnership offers, general feedback.
options.name: other

questions.instructions: How urgently does this message need a reply? Judge by business impact and how blocked the customer is, not by how upset the writer sounds.

options.description: Nobody is blocked. Can wait several days.
options.name: low

options.description: A real problem with a workaround, or a routine request. Answer within a day.
options.name: normal

options.description: The customer is blocked from using the product, or money is at stake. Answer within hours.
options.name: high

options.description: Widespread outage, data loss, or legal and financial exposure. Answer immediately.
options.name: critical

questions.instructions: Does this message need a human agent, rather than an automated reply or a help-centre article?

options.description: It needs judgement, an account change, or a back-and-forth conversation.
options.name: yes

options.description: A templated answer or a help-centre link would fully resolve it.
options.name: no
